expense_categories.description: Anything that doesn't clearly fit the categories above. Prefer a clarifying question over guessing into this bucket when confidence is low.

sales_categories.description: Invoiced or cash sale of goods/services to a customer. Phase 1 has a single revenue account -- no sub-categorisation by product line or tax treatment yet (Vol 6_1 Section 4).

purchase_categories.description: Goods or raw materials purchased for resale or direct use in producing what the business sells (Vol 6_2 Section 4 capitalisation-vs-expense distinction).
Office supplies, consumables, small tools bought from a supplier.
Premises or equipment rental billed via a supplier/purchase relationship.
Electricity, water, internet, phone billed as a supplier purchase.
Advertising, promotions, sponsored content bought from a supplier.
Anything purchased that doesn't clearly fit the categories above. Prefer a clarifying question over guessing into this bucket when confidence is low.

rules.description: An Expense Business Event with a clearly matched vendor and a single line amount classifies directly against the matching category above.
rules.output: LedgerEntry: debit matched Operating Expenses category, credit Cash/Bank (or Accounts Payable if payment_method is unspecified/deferred)

rules.description: If the vendor has a Business Knowledge trusted mapping (Vol 4_2 Section 3.1, 3+ confirmations), use that category and raise confidence rather than reclassifying from scratch.
A Sales Business Event (Invoice Issued) classifies against Sales Revenue -- Phase 1's only revenue account. Revenue is recognised on invoice basis (Vol 6_1 Section 4 default), not payment basis.
rules.output: LedgerEntry: debit Cash/Bank (paid immediately) or Accounts Receivable (payment_method unspecified/deferred, i.e. sold on credit), credit Sales Revenue

rules.description: A Purchase Business Event (Supplier Bill / Goods Received) with a clearly matched category classifies against the matching Cost of Goods Sold or Operating Expenses category above (Vol 6_2 Section 4 capitalisation-vs-expense distinction, approximated in Phase 1 without a formal inventory ledger).
rules.output: LedgerEntry: debit matched category, credit Cash/Bank (paid immediately) or Accounts Payable (payment_method unspecified/deferred)

rules.description: If the supplier has a Business Knowledge trusted mapping (Vol 4_2 Section 3.1, 3+ confirmations), use that category and raise confidence rather than reclassifying from scratch.

A Bank Fee event classifies against Operating Expenses:Bank Fees. Deposit/Withdrawal events matched to an existing outstanding receivable/payable settle that item's Accounts Receivable/Payable balance; unmatched Deposit/Withdrawal events post against Owner's Equity / Drawings as a generic capital-in/out placeholder. Applied deterministically in app/src/db/bankingRepository.ts (Sprint 7) -- Banking is manual-entry only in Phase 1 (Vol 0_1 Section 4), so this rule is not run through the AI classification pipeline the way EXP/SALE/PUR rules are; it is recorded here for governance/audit provenance, not runtime PCB assembly.
rules.output: see description -- posting shape depends on transaction_type and whether a reconciliation match was made

rules.description: The unit price used for a product on any document (quotation, invoice, etc.) resolves in order: (1) the party's own assigned price type, if it has an effective PriceListEntry for this product; (2) the business's default price type's effective PriceListEntry for this product, used whenever step 1 doesn't apply -- either because the party has no price type assigned, or its assigned price type exists but has no effective entry for this specific product (this second fallback case is a disclosed extension beyond Vol 13_0 Section 5's literal two-step wording, added so a party with a price type that simply hasn't been given an entry for a given product still gets a usable price instead of a hard failure); (3) if neither resolves, no price is returned and the caller must raise a clarify/error, never silently default to 0 or null. 'Effective' means effective_from <= today and (effective_to is null or effective_to >= today), preferring the most recent effective_from when more than one entry qualifies. Applied deterministically in public.resolve_price (Sprint 27) -- price resolution is not run through the AI classification pipeline the way EXP/SALE/PUR rules are; it is recorded here for governance/audit provenance, not runtime PCB assembly.
rules.applies_when: domain_hint == 'pricing' || resolving a unit_price for a product+party pair on any outbound document
rules.output: unit_price, price_type_id, price_list_entry_id, used_business_default -- see public.resolve_price's return shape

limitations: Banking domain (Sprint 7) is manual-entry only, deterministic (not AI-classified) -- Deposit, Withdrawal, Bank Fee are covered; Transfer is recorded for audit trail but posts no ledger entries, since Phase 1 has a single undifferentiated Cash/Bank account (Vol 11_1 Section 4.1) and a transfer between the business's own accounts is invisible to a single-account model. Reconciliation (matching a Deposit/Withdrawal to an outstanding receivable/payable) supports full-amount settlement only -- partial payment against an invoice/bill is not yet supported.
Sales domain in Phase 1 has a single revenue category (Sales Revenue) -- no sub-categorisation, ageing, or tax treatment yet (Vol 6_1 Section 4/5).

Payment Received (full settlement of an outstanding receivable/payable via a matched Banking Deposit/Withdrawal, Vol 6_1 Section 6, Vol 6_4) is implemented as of Sprint 7. Partial settlement (paying part of an invoice/bill) is NOT implemented -- a match requires the Deposit/Withdrawal amount to equal the outstanding balance exactly.

Purchase domain's capitalisation-vs-expense distinction (Vol 6_2 Section 4) is approximated by a flat category match (Operating Expenses:* or Cost of Goods Sold) -- no formal inventory/asset ledger yet (Vol 6_5, Phase 3).
This bundle does not provide tax-filing advice; see Vol 6_9 Section 5.
Payroll, inventory, and asset domains are explicitly out of Phase 1 scope (Vol 0_1).
Overdue receivables (Vol 0_1 Section 6) are approximated by a captured_at-age threshold, not a real invoice due date -- Phase 1's BusinessData schema has no due-date field (Vol 11_1 Section 3).

Pricing (Sprint 27) covers manual per-product-per-price-type prices only -- cost_source 'auto_from_purchase' on public.products is stubbed and rejected server-side until the Purchase module addendum ships; promo_note on a PriceListEntry is a bare text field, not a structured promotion/discount engine.
